executiveSummary: GM0415's identity, Veiligheidsregio Zaanstreek-Waterland assignment, full 2025 boundary and CBS resident control are coherent. Fresh context reports 11,745 residents; ten published neighbourhood rows sum to 11,750 (+5, +0.043%), a negligible difference that retains CBS rounding and suppression semantics. The bundle contains three districts, ten neighbourhoods, three BAG places, three BRT woonkernen, no ProRail station and 29 scheduled-transit stop areas. All ten canonical presets execute deterministically at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across eight services and pass structural/numerical contracts. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Landsmeer is a low peat-polder municipality in Waterland, where protected-polder flooding after a defence breach, Markermeer/IJsselmeer effects on buitendijkse areas, Schermerboezem or regional-kade problems, and local cluster-rain/sewer-pump overload are distinct mechanisms. The generic coastal preset applies 1.526111 normalized inundation stress at T+24 to 6,957 residents and leaves 857 affected at T+72 without a selected defence/breach, footprint, polder/peilgebied, arrival or recession; the value is never 1.53 physical metres. The river preset returns exact zero but only tests its configured narrow source, not Waterland safety. Seven unrelated single hazards plus compound reuse exactly the same complete neighbourhood order, placing five-resident Sportpark first while nature/recreation area Twiske remains near the bottom. The transport graph has zero logical routes despite public roads, 29 stops, an Amsterdam concession and cross-boundary acute-care dependence. Exact utility, mobility, care, supply and recovery trajectories therefore lack topology, capacity, backup, incident state, resources and actions. Empty warning, road, forecast, acute-care, air, seismic and government-service screens are Unknown/NoData, never zero or safe.

evidenceSources.title: E01 — Kerncijfers wijken en buurten 2025, table 86165NED, OData API
supports: The official municipality row identifies GM0415 Landsmeer and reports 11,745 residents, density 523 per square kilometre, 23.5% age 65 or older and 1,514 one-person households.

The ten published neighbourhood rows sum to 11,750 residents (+5, +0.043%), 5,040 households and 2,765 residents aged 65 or older; the negligible difference retains annual rounding and suppression semantics.

Most fields cover all ten neighbourhoods; home-value, tenure, cars per household, benefits, GP/supermarket distance and density cover eight, while district-heating share and public-charging counts cover zero and must not become zero.

CBS OData is machine-readable under CC BY 4.0, with quarterly additions described for this annual table. It controls residents, not incident-time visitors, patients, pupils, commuters, responders, livestock, shelter occupancy, self-reliance or preparedness.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Waterland peilgebieden, boezem and calamity mechanisms with public water-asset registry
evidenceSources.edition: Current peilbesluit/calammity pages; historic Watergebiedsplan De Waterlanden dated 1 June 2013; HWH snapshot retrieved 3 September 2026
supports: HHNK publishes adopted peilbesluiten with target levels and margins per area. Its older Watergebiedsplan De Waterlanden demonstrates distinct peat-polder and peilgebied contexts for Twiske, Purmerland and Waterland but is historic context and must not override current decisions.

HHNK explains that polders discharge excess water to boezem canals and that regional and primary defences protect land from polder/boezem and IJsselmeer/Markermeer pathways. Extreme polder inundation and sewer pump/pressure-main failure are separate calamity mechanisms.

The deployment registry returns 85 municipal points: five sewer pumps, 34 surface-water pumps, one sluice and 45 weirs. It is a partial/contributor-dependent national aggregation under CC BY-SA 4.0 and does not provide catchment/topology, comparable capacity, settings, power/backup, maintenance or live operation.
Target water levels and registered assets are static context, not achieved incident water levels, defence condition, pump command, remaining storage or flood forecasts.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2025–2028, crisis publications and 72-hour preparedness
evidenceSources.edition: Risk profile valid from 19 December 2024; policy plan 2025–2028; crisis plan 2026–2029; national guidance current at access
supports: The current risk profile distinguishes a primary-defence breach, Markermeer rise flooding buitendijkse areas while the primary defence remains safe, and a local cluster cloudburst. Its examples are explicitly illustrative, not selected incidents or local calibrations.

It identifies extreme rain/drought, dike cracking, nature/berm fire, heat pressure on care and water/electricity demand, blocked routes, electricity/telecom/drainage cascades, drink-water contamination, gas interruption, cyber disruption and care continuity as relevant regional mechanisms.

A primary-defence breach can flood a large area within hours, take days to close and much longer to recover. That planning example does not identify a Landsmeer defence section, breach, flood course or exercise state.
Regional policy/crisis plans define governance, roles and possible activation, not live staff, resources, shelter, warning, action, operator state or restoration commitments.

National guidance advises a 72-hour emergency kit including three litres of water per person per day, food, medicine, radio/power and a personal plan. Guidance does not prove household readiness or local supply availability.

supports: LIWO 2025.1.6 provides professional flood layers requiring expert water-manager interpretation. A selected case must retain source, defence/breach/control state, protected versus buitendijkse domain, footprint, native units/resolution, arrival/persistence/recession, probability, CRS, licence and NoData.
No Waterinfo observation or forecast point is assigned inside GM0415. Missing point coverage cannot establish current polder, boezem, Markermeer or sewer state and cannot be propagated through T+72.

The 48-hour KNMI province-warning retrieval has no warning records, and the NDW 72-hour current-situation snapshot assigns no road situation inside GM0415. These issue-time coverage results do not validate arbitrary exercise forcing or prove roads open.

KNMI sources are CC BY 4.0 and Waterinfo/NDW CC0 unless stated. Every operational record needs issue, observation, valid and retrieval time, spatial support, revision/fault state and affectsSimulation.
